<section id="executive-summary"><h2>01. Executive Summary</h2>
<p><strong>Infinity Living Options</strong> proposes a rapid, flood-resilient, and earthquake-safe transitional housing solution using factory-manufactured Light Gauge Steel (LGS) modules on helical screw pile foundations for disaster recovery in West Sumatra and across Indonesia.</p>
<h3>Value Proposition</h3>
<ul>
<li>30 m² family units installed in <strong>3.5–5 days</strong></li>
<li>Elevated 600–900 mm above flood zones on helical screw piles</li>
<li>Measurable quality control — torque logged on every pile</li>
<li>Reusable and relocatable design — no concrete foundations</li>
<li>Factory capacity: <strong>50–75 units/month</strong></li>
</ul>
<h3>Pricing Summary</h3>
<table><thead><tr><th>Option</th><th>Description</th><th>Unit Price (IDR)</th><th>USD</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>A</td><td>Rapid Shelter — basic envelope, minimal electrical</td><td>Rp 274,784,666</td><td>$18,319</td></tr>
<tr><td>B</td><td>Family Unit — full MEP, partitions, upgraded envelope</td><td>Rp 398,625,040</td><td>$26,575</td></tr>
<tr><td>C</td><td>Clinic / Command Hub — enhanced MEP</td><td>Rp 504,656,425</td><td>$33,644</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
<h3>Track Record</h3>
<p>141+ buildings | 15,000+ m² | 95% on-time delivery | Banyuwangi factory producing 150 tonnes LGS/month.</p>
</section>

<section id="technical-proposal"><h2>03. Technical Proposal</h2>
<h3>Shelter Typologies</h3>
<table><thead><tr><th>Option</th><th>Description</th><th>Size</th><th>Price (IDR)</th></tr></thead><tbody>

</tbody></table>

<h3>Structural System — Light Gauge Steel (LGS)</h3>
<p>Factory-manufactured Cold-Formed Steel framing using Howick FRAMA 3200 roll formers with Vertex BD BIM software. <span class="tag tag-source">Source: technical-specifications.html</span></p>
<table><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Specification</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>Steel Grade</td><td>G550 (550 MPa yield)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Thickness</td><td>0.75 mm – 1.2 mm</td></tr>
<tr><td>Coating</td><td>Z275 galvanized (275 g/m²)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Connections</td><td>Self-drilling screws (~12,000/unit)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Frame Weight</td><td>~850 kg per unit</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
<p><span class="tag tag-assume">ASSUMPTION: Strategy document references AZ150 — coating standard requires clarification</span></p>

<h3>Foundation System — Helical Screw Piles</h3>
<p>Engineered for peat, swamp, and flood zones. End-bearing through helical plates in deep stable strata.</p>
<table><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Specification</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>Type</td><td>Round/square shaft, 1–3 helix plates</td></tr>
<tr><td>Quantity</td><td>10–14 piles per unit</td></tr>
<tr><td>Material</td><td>Hot-dip galvanized steel (610 g/m²)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Standard</td><td>ICC-ES AC358; ASTM A123/A123M</td></tr>
<tr><td>Capacity</td><td>10–40+ tonnes (compression)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Extensions</td><td>Modular 1.5 m / 2 m sections</td></tr>
<tr><td>Design Life</td><td>25+ years (with maintenance)</td></tr>
<tr><td>QA</td><td>Torque logging every pile + 2–5% proof load testing</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
<p><span class="tag tag-assume">ASSUMPTION: Foundation design based on generic peat/alluvial soil profiles. Site-specific geotechnical investigation required.</span></p>

<h3>Performance Standards</h3>
<table><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Standard</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>Thermal</td><td>R-value 2.5–3.0 m²K/W (ISO 6946)</td></tr>
<tr><td>Air Infiltration</td><td>&lt; 5.0 m³/h·m² @ 50 Pa (ASTM E779)</td></tr>

<section id="qaqc"><h2>05. QA/QC Plan</h2>
<h3>Material Receipt</h3>
<ul><li>Verify steel mill certificates (G550, Z275 coating)</li><li>Visual inspection for coating damage</li><li>Dimensional verification of sample LGS profiles</li><li>Verify helical pile certification (ICC-ES AC358)</li><li>Check pile galvanization coating (610 g/m²)</li></ul>
<h3>Roll Forming / Fabrication</h3>
<ul><li>Verify profile dimensions against Vertex BD output</li><li>Check cutting tolerances (±1 mm)</li><li>Inspect pre-punched holes for accuracy</li><li>Verify component marking and labeling</li></ul>
<h3>Installation Checks</h3>
<ul><li>Torque logging on every helical pile installed</li><li>2–5% proof load testing on helical piles</li><li>Pile depth and elevation verification</li><li>Frame squareness and level checks</li><li>Frame connection torque verification</li><li>Envelope weather-tightness inspection</li><li>MEP testing (electrical, plumbing)</li></ul>
<h3>Final Handover</h3>
<ul><li>Comprehensive visual inspection</li><li>Complete handover checklist</li><li>As-built documentation package</li><li>Torque logs and proof load reports</li><li>Completion certificate</li><li>Maintenance manual and schedule</li><li>12-month warranty activation</li></ul>
</section>
<section id="hse"><h2>06. Health, Safety & Environment Plan</h2>
<p><span class="tag tag-assume">ASSUMPTION: Generic HSE plan — no specific HSE policy document in workspace</span></p>
<h3>Site Hazards</h3>
<ul><li>Uneven surfaces and soft ground (peat/swamp)</li><li>Flood risk and standing water</li><li>Hazardous fauna at remote sites</li><li>Heat exposure / high humidity</li><li>Limited access / distance from medical facilities</li></ul>
<h3>Working at Height</h3>
<ul><li>All work above 1.8 m requires fall arrest</li><li>Scaffolding inspected before use</li><li>Roof installation requires harness + anchor points</li></ul>
<h3>PPE Requirements</h3>
<ul><li>Safety helmet — mandatory in all construction areas</li><li>Steel-toe boots — mandatory</li><li>Hi-vis vest — mandatory</li><li>Work gloves — when handling steel</li><li>Safety glasses — when cutting/drilling</li><li>Hearing protection — loud tools</li><li>Harness — working at height &gt;1.8 m</li></ul>
<h3>Incident Reporting</h3>
<ul><li>All incidents reported within 24 hours to HSE Manager</li><li>Near-misses reported and investigated</li><li>Root cause investigation for significant incidents</li><li>Weekly HSE review during construction</li></ul>
</section>

<section id="method-statements"><h2>09. Method Statements</h2>
<h3>A. Helical Screw Pile Installation</h3>
<h4>Equipment Required</h4>
<ul><li>Mini-excavator with hydraulic torque head</li><li>Survey equipment (level, total station)</li><li>Digital torque logger</li><li>Pile extension sections (1.5 m / 2 m)</li></ul>
<h4>Procedure</h4>
<ol>
<li>Set out pile grid per foundation drawing</li>
<li>Position excavator and attach torque head</li>
<li>Place first helical pile vertically at marked point</li>
<li>Begin rotation — monitor torque and penetration rate</li>
<li>Add extension sections to reach stable strata</li>
<li>Record final torque when target reached</li>
<li>Cut pile to design elevation</li>
<li>Install pile cap / bracket</li>
<li>Repeat for all piles</li>
</ol>
<h4>Quality Control</h4>
<ul><li>Torque recorded for 100% of piles</li><li>Proof load testing on 2–5% of piles</li><li>Depth and elevation verification</li><li>Visual inspection of galvanized coating</li></ul>

<h3>B. LGS Modular Assembly</h3>
<h4>Work Sequence</h4>
<ol>
<li>Install steel floor chassis onto pile caps — bolt to brackets</li>
<li>Lay floor panels onto chassis</li>
<li>Lift and bolt prefabricated wall panels</li>
<li>Install roof frame on top of walls</li>
<li>Fix metal roofing — ensure overlap and sealant</li>
<li>Install wall cladding</li>
<li>Fit doors and windows</li>
<li>Run electrical wiring and plumbing</li>
<li>Final inspection and handover</li>
</ol>
<h4>Safety</h4>
<ul><li>Harness mandatory during roof installation</li><li>Exclusion zone during panel lifting</li><li>Full PPE at all times</li><li>Daily safety briefing</li></ul>
</section>
